statements.proposition: This change modifies the --global path resolution in Library/Homebrew/bundle/brewfile.rb to choose between XDG and legacy paths, without changing behaviour for existing setups.
statements.label: TRUE
statements.note: brewfile.rb is modified. Base vs head case analysis: in non-XDG mode (HOMEBREW_USER_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/.homebrew, which does not end with '/homebrew') the old branches are untouched. In XDG mode, an existing XDG Brewfile is still used and an existing ~/.Brewfile is still used. Only the case where neither file exists changes: the XDG path is returned instead of ~/.Brewfile, which is the intended fix. Settled by reading the code, not by running it.

statements.note: Two specs were added, both for the 'neither Brewfile exists' case, so that part is true. 'All backwards compatibility scenarios' is not: no spec covers the key case (XDG mode, legacy ~/.Brewfile exists). Also, every spec uses HOMEBREW_USER_CONFIG_HOME='/Users/username/.homebrew', which does not end with '/homebrew', so the new XDG branch (using_xdg) is never entered by any spec. The added 'XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set' spec stubs ENV['XDG_CONFIG_HOME'], which the code does not read. I did not run the specs.
